messages.subject: inspect variables in 'model' block
parts:
I have a HMM with forward-backward model as shown below. I wish to inspect the posterior p(z_n|Data) where z_n is the state assignment variable. However, considering that p[N,K] is local to the `model` block I won't end up seeing this as one of the output parameters. How do you go about ensuring this will get saved?

Incase I don't really care about saving the entire chain but just want the mean of it, how would I cater for that case? Saving a NxK matrix for a large chain might not be the best idea.

Side note: I've declared mu as a ordered variable in the hope that it solves/ masks the multimodal issue.


model {
    real acc[K];
    real lg_alpha[N,K];
    real lg_beta[N,K];
    real p[N,K];
    
    //Prior distributions
    for (k in 1:K){
        sigma[k] ~ exponential(0.1);
        mu[k] ~ normal(0.0,5.0);
    }
    // Forward step
    for (k in 1:K)
        lg_alpha[1,k] <- normal_log(y[n],mu[k],sigma[k]);
    for (t in 2:N) {
        for (k in 1:K) {
            for (j in 1:K)
                acc[j] <- lg_alpha[t-1,j] + log(theta[j,k]) + normal_log(y[n],mu[k],sigma[k]);
            lg_alpha[t,k] <- log_sum_exp(acc);
        } 
    }
    lg_X = log_sum_exp(lg_alpha[N])
    increment_log_prob(lg_X);
    
    
    // Backward step
    for (k in 1:K)
        lg_beta[N,k] <- 0.0;
    for (t in 1:(N-1)) {
        for (k in 1:K) {
            for (j in 1:K)
                acc[j] <- lg_beta[N-t+1,j] + log(theta[k,j]) + normal_log(y[n],mu[j],sigma[j]);
            lg_beta[N-t,k] <- log_sum_exp(acc);
        } 
    }
    
    for (t in 1:N){
        for (k in 1:K){
            p[t,k]=exp(lg_alpha[t,k]+lg_beta[t,k]-lg_X);
        }
    }
    
}

messages.subject: Re: inspect variables in 'model' block
parts:
On Thursday, April 7, 2016 at 2:51:26 AM UTC-4, Sachinthaka Abeywardana wrote:
I have a HMM with forward-backward model as shown below. I wish to inspect the posterior p(z_n|Data) where z_n is the state assignment variable. However, considering that p[N,K] is local to the `model` block I won't end up seeing this as one of the output parameters. How do you go about ensuring this will get saved?

Incase I don't really care about saving the entire chain but just want the mean of it, how would I cater for that case? Saving a NxK matrix for a large chain might not be the best idea.

Side note: I've declared mu as a ordered variable in the hope that it solves/ masks the multimodal issue.

If you are using rstan, you can
  • define p in transformed parameters
  • not save the draws of p by calling stan with pars = "p", include = FALSE
  • use get_posterior_mean() afterward to look at the posterior mean of everything, including p

Ben
